title: Refactor adapter defaults into method-specific PEFT YAML groups
description: Split the shared adapter/PEFT shell settings from method-specific adapter settings in Hydra config. Keep the user-facing shape as adapter.peft.<method>: {...}, keep branch presence as the normal method selection rule, and move method defaults into method-local YAML files such as configs/_defaults/adapter/peft/lora.yaml and configs/_defaults/adapter/peft/loha.yaml. The default adapter config should still compose a concrete active method instead of leaving adapter mode without method settings.

title: Move method-specific adapter validation out of generic PEFT validation
description: Remove adapter-specific LoHa checks from library/config/config_validation.py. Validation for active adapter branches should flow through method-owned config binding/runtime translation rather than hardcoded adapter names in shared validation. As part of this cleanup, stop relying on LoHa module constructor defaults when adapter.peft.loha.rank is unset; require method-owned config translation to define or reject rank explicitly.

title: Reconcile LoHa bypass-mode with weight decomposition
description: Fix the semantic mismatch between bypass_mode and weight_decompose for the repo-owned LoHa path. Vendored LyCORIS disables bypass mode when DoRA-style weight decomposition is enabled, but the absorbed implementation currently lets bypass_mode win and silently skip the decomposition path. Decide the intended repo-owned behavior, validate incompatible config combinations, and add focused coverage.

title: Validate required LoHa rank in config and runtime
description: Fix the active LoHa rank gap: adapter.peft.loha.rank currently defaults to None while the absorbed LoHa module requires a positive integer rank. Add validation and/or sane defaults so empty or malformed LoHa config fails clearly before runtime construction, and ensure the forward config surface documents whether rank is required or defaulted.

title: Promote PEFT under adapter config and mode
description: Refactor adapter training so PEFT is represented as one adapter family under the adapter concept instead of the root training mode/config surface. Target shape is mode: adapter with adapter.peft.<method> branch selection, avoiding redundant adapter.type and peft.method discriminators when the active branch already names the family/method. Validate exactly one active adapter family and exactly one active PEFT method, then update runtime wiring, Hydra defaults, tests, docs, and compatibility handling as needed.

title: Design a stronger config validation workflow
description: The roadmap calls out config validation as an active TODO. Create a focused follow-up to define how invalid configs should be caught, where validation should live, and what should be covered by tests versus runtime checks. This should produce a concrete plan for validation ownership and the highest-risk missing validations in the active training/config surface.

title: Add OFT parity fixtures and extra coverage
description: Follow up on the repo-owned OFT implementation with real checkpoint interoperability coverage and a few method-specific regression cases that were deferred from the implementation pass.
acceptance_criteria: Add at least one real or fixture-based OFT checkpoint parity test covering repo-owned load/export semantics against absorbed LyCORIS/HF expectations.; Add focused OFT tests for at least one currently untested edge area such as Conv1d/Conv3d, max-norm behavior, or additional bypass/dropout semantics.; Document any confirmed OFT-specific compatibility limits or semantic differences in library/adapters/methods/peft/README.md if parity work uncovers them.
notes: Repo guidance: this stabilization work is intended as an immediate follow-up to the initial OFT landing. Also note that the repo does not currently need to preserve backward compatibility for an early OFT checkpoint/layout choice; compatibility import/export helpers can be added separately later without constraining the core training pipeline design now.

title: Absorb OFT adapter method into repo-owned PEFT layer
description: Add repo-owned OFT support under library/adapters/methods/peft/oft using the established PEFT-family ownership model, with config/runtime/state-dict integration, tests, and docs. Vendor LyCORIS should be treated as the algorithm reference, but repo-owned implementation should fix issues or improve behavior where the absorbed design suggests it.

title: Absorb LoCon into repo-owned PEFT adapter layer
description: Add repo-owned LoCon under adapter.peft.locon by adapting vendored LyCORIS behavior into the current PEFT method structure, with config/runtime/state-dict/tests/docs updates.

title: Absorb LoCon adapter method into repo-owned PEFT layer
description: Add repo-owned LoCon support under library/adapters/methods/peft/locon using the established PEFT-family ownership model, with config/runtime/state-dict integration, tests, and docs.

title: Move PEFT method config resolution out of adapter root
description: Refactor adapter config resolution so PEFT-family method branch selection and runtime-spec translation live under library/adapters/methods/peft rather than library/adapters/. Keep the root adapter layer focused on generic runtime lookup/build concerns.
close_reason: Moved PEFT-family method resolution out of library/adapters and into library/adapters/methods/peft, updating callers accordingly.

title: Move adapter method registration ownership out of root adapter registry
description: Clean up adapter method registration/config resolution so method packages own their registration metadata and root adapter code derives method branch keys from registrations instead of accumulating method-specific literals.
close_reason: Moved PEFT method registration metadata into method packages and made config resolution derive method branches from registrations.

title: Absorb LoKr adapter method into repo-owned PEFT layer
description: Bring LoKr capability over from the vendored LyCORIS implementation into the repo-owned adapter method layer, add validation/runtime/state-dict support, focused tests, and capture useful implementation insights for future PEFT method shape.
close_reason: Implemented repo-owned LoKr PEFT method runtime/config/state-dict support with focused tests and docs notes.

title: Decide long-term LoHa weight_decompose and bypass_mode semantics
description: Current repo-owned LoHa rejects weight_decompose=True together with bypass_mode=True to avoid silently skipping DoRA behavior. Follow up by deciding the intended long-term semantics: keep rejection, mirror LyCORIS by auto-disabling bypass when DoRA is enabled, or define a repo-owned combined behavior. Include config-surface guidance and test coverage for the chosen rule.

title: Define and implement plain dropout semantics for LoHa
description: Clarify what the forward LoHa dropout knob should mean in this repo. Vendored LyCORIS only partially wires plain dropout through bypass-mode behavior and warns that normal LoHa dropout is not really implemented, while the absorbed implementation currently exposes the field without applying it. Decide whether to support vendor-style bypass dropout, define a cleaner repo-owned behavior, or deprecate/remove the field in favor of rank_dropout and module_dropout.

title: Define and implement plain dropout semantics for LoHa
description: Clarify what the forward LoHa  knob should mean in this repo. Vendored LyCORIS only partially wires plain dropout through bypass-mode behavior and warns that normal LoHa dropout is not really implemented, while the absorbed implementation currently exposes the field without applying it. Decide whether to support vendor-style bypass dropout, define a cleaner repo-owned behavior, or deprecate/remove the field in favor of rank_dropout and module_dropout.

title: Design versioned multi-method adapter artifact format
description: Design a repo-owned saved-adapter artifact format that can eventually hold multiple adapter methods in one file. Define the manifest/versioning story, how method type and method-local settings are represented, how target identity is recorded, and how tensor namespaces should be structured so future LoHa/LoRA/etc. payloads can coexist without relying purely on flat tensor-name conventions.

title: Investigate and document "full bf16" semantics
description: The roadmap explicitly calls out uncertainty around what "full bf16" means in this repo. Audit the active code/config paths that mention or imply full-bf16 behavior, identify the current effective behavior, and document the intended meaning and any mismatches. The outcome should reduce ambiguity for future precision-related refactors and validation work.

title: Add PEFT per-component diagnostics breakdown
description: Implement the deferred PEFT diagnostics follow-up from the roadmap. Add an optional adapter protocol method such as get_diagnostics_components() so adapter types can report their per-component module and parameter allocation, then thread that data into PeftMode training diagnostics without reopening old compatibility-era runtime boundaries.

title: Continue strategy-system follow-up cleanup
description: Track the remaining strategy-system cleanup called out in the roadmap: SD / SDXL cleanup against the settled base contract, review of contracts.py naming/organization, concrete or compatibility unet-to-denoiser follow-up where it still makes architectural sense, and moving model-specific behavior lower when it still sits too high in base/. Use the existing docs_design strategy follow-up notes as supporting context.

title: Evaluate compact OFT upper-triangle parameterization
description: Review whether the repo-owned OFT implementation should switch from storing full square block parameters to storing only the independent upper-triangular values, similar to Hugging Face PEFT's OFT rotation module, while preserving our LyCORIS-aligned Diag-OFT behavior and checkpoint compatibility expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Compare current repo-owned OFT parameter count and checkpoint layout against an upper-triangle-only design.; Decide whether the memory/compute savings justify the extra reconstruction complexity for this repo.; If adopted, preserve or explicitly migrate repo-owned OFT checkpoint compatibility and document the decision in library/adapters/methods/peft/README.md and CHANGELOG.md as appropriate.
notes: Repo guidance: there is currently no meaningful backward-compatibility pressure for repo-owned OFT checkpoints or parameter layouts. Prefer the best native design for this repo first; if old/full-block import support is ever needed later, keep it as explicit compatibility helpers outside the core training pipeline rather than shaping the training/runtime design now. This should be treated as an immediate follow-up after the current OFT landing work, not as distant backlog.

title: Revert benchmark test relaxation
description: Revert the dataloader throughput benchmark relaxations and related changelog note because the changes weakened the signal.

title: Stabilize dataloader benchmark throughput test
description: Adjust the mocked-I/O dataloader throughput benchmark so ordinary local/unit runs do not fail on machine-dependent wall-clock variance while preserving a strict opt-in benchmark threshold.

title: Finish strict LoRA-family move out of adapter root
description: Remove restored root shims for lora/dylora/oft/lora_utils/lora_diffusers, update tests to patch/import the new method-package paths directly, and revert the unrelated benchmark-threshold relaxation.

title: Restore adapter root shims after PEFT method-file moves
description: Re-add root compatibility shims for lora/dylora/oft plus lora_utils/lora_diffusers after moving ownership under the PEFT method package, and relax local benchmark throughput gating while keeping strict mode opt-in.

title: Restore LoRA utility compatibility shims after method-folder move
description: Re-add root adapter shim modules for lora_utils and lora_diffusers so legacy imports, tool scripts, and unittest.patch paths keep working after moving ownership under library/adapters/methods/peft/lora/.

title: Fix adapter regression tests after LoHa/LoKr validation changes
description: Update adapter/training tests to match stricter repo-owned LoHa validation and avoid rewriting mapped safetensors files in place on Windows-style temp paths.

title: Harden LoKr dtype handling and explicit factor semantics
description: Make repo-owned LoKr forward paths robust to mixed input/weight dtypes and preserve explicit factor orientation when factorization is requested.

title: Review Hugging Face PEFT LoKr for improvement candidates
description: Compare the current upstream PEFT LoKr tuner against our repo-owned LoKr implementation and capture concrete improvement opportunities or reasons to stay different.

title: Document adapter and PEFT layer ownership notes
description: Add short repo-owned guidance notes under library/adapters and library/adapters/methods/peft so future work keeps family/method-specific logic out of the adapter upper layer.

title: Explore multi-method PEFT capability within adapter families
description: Explore support for training runs that combine multiple PEFT adapter methods within the same adapter family, especially LyCORIS-shaped combinations. Keep the normal single-method adapter.peft.<method> config path simple, but investigate whether repo-owned helpers or composition seams should support multi-method PEFT runs in the future. This should stay scoped to adapter-family combinations rather than generic cross-family adapter mixing unless a stronger use case appears.

title: Explore method resolution and optimizer grouping for mixed-method adapters
description: Follow up on how adapter method resolution, target ownership, and optimizer grouping should work if a future adapter-family helper can combine multiple PEFT methods in one run. Clarify which method owns each target, how trainable refs and grouping plans should be attributed, and what defaults or helper-owned rules should apply to optimization groups when methods differ.

title: Add shared adapter runtime state controls
description: Explore shared adapter runtime controls that will matter once the repo supports richer saved-adapter artifacts and multiple logical payloads. Consider lightweight enable/disable behavior, explicit reversible merge/unmerge operations, and any minimal active-state concepts needed for future multi-method or multi-payload adapter runtimes without importing PEFT's full wrapper model.

title: Improve adapter load diagnostics and target mismatch reporting
description: Improve repo-owned adapter load/reporting so failures are easier to reason about when target resolution and saved tensors diverge. Cover cases like unsupported targets skipped during load, target names present in a checkpoint but absent from the current model, shape mismatches, and partial method payloads. Prefer shared adapter-loader diagnostics where possible so the behavior benefits more than just LoHa.

title: Expand behavioral test coverage for repo-owned LoHa
description: Broaden focused LoHa test coverage beyond the current linear/tucker round-trip cases. Add behavior tests for Conv1d and Conv3d targets, rs_lora scaling, weight_decompose, wd_on_output=False, bypass_mode, rank_dropout scaling, module dropout, and any finalized plain-dropout behavior. Keep the coverage centered on repo-owned semantics rather than PEFT/LyCORIS parity for its own sake.

title: Document OpenSpec and beads workflow in AGENTS
description: Add AGENTS.md guidance describing when to use OpenSpec versus beads, and clarify that OpenSpec artifacts complement rather than replace bd issue tracking.

title: Document regularization-image usage constraints
description: The roadmap notes that the current reg_data_dir / is_reg flow is mechanically correct but easy to misuse. Add a docs-focused follow-up to explain that regularization images only help when they are genuine class/prior images with matching generic captions or class_tokens, and make sure future examples communicate that clearly.

title: Add adapter diagnostics for method-specific runtime stats
description: Backlog adapter-systems follow-up: decide whether the repo should surface more adapter diagnostics in training/reporting, such as per-component module counts, parameter totals, or method-specific norm summaries. This should be treated as shared adapter infrastructure rather than a LoHa-only requirement, and it should stay secondary to correctness and artifact-format work.

title: Make LoHa initialization policy explicit
description: Consider making LoHa initialization an explicit repo-owned policy rather than an implicit carry-over from the absorbed LyCORIS behavior. The immediate goal is not PEFT parity, but clearer ownership: document the current initialization choice, decide whether the repo wants named init modes or one fixed policy, and add tests that pin the intended behavior if this is judged worth keeping configurable.

title: Evaluate extracting a dedicated LoHa functional kernel layer
description: Backlog investigation: decide whether the repo-owned LoHa math should stay embedded in the module wrapper or move into a more isolated functional layer. This is low priority and should only move forward if profiling, autograd debugging, or method sharing across runtimes makes the extra indirection worthwhile.
